episodes.184437: A strong low pressure system dropped into the Great Basin. This led to a tightening southwest gradient over western Colorado and breezy conditions. Additionally, moisture out ahead of the system produced isolated showers and thunderstorms which led to even gustier winds. Some outflow from decaying thunderstorms generated wind gusts in excess of 58 mph in portions of Garfield County.
episodes.184488: Severe storms developed over portions of eastern NM. One strong storm dropped nickel sized hail in Colfax County in the afternoon. Later in the evening, two severe storms produced strong wind gusts at the Tucumcari and Roswell airport observing sites.
episodes.184910: Gusty winds were observed in many locations around Utah as precipitation began ahead of an approaching system.
episodes.185581: Afternoon thunderstorms ahead of a cold front moving south across southwest Florida produce a funnel cloud over Estero Bay near Fort Myers Beach in Lee County.
episodes.185676: A large trough across the western CONUS helped initiate thunderstorms across the western higher elevations. Locally strong to severe winds were observed with these thunderstorms.
episodes.185677: A large trough across the western CONUS helped initiate thunderstorms across the western higher elevations. Locally strong to severe winds were observed with these thunderstorms.
episodes.185843: Outer bands from Tropical Storm Philippe, which passed northeast of the islands resulted in heavy rain, river rises, lightning strikes and flooding across various sectors of the islands. Around up to 5 to 10 inches of rain fell over mainly eastern Puerto Rico from Oct 1st through October 5th.
episodes.186080: An upper low was moving into California with strong southwest flow ahead of it across the Borderland.  A weak surface trough helped to trigger isolated thunderstorms around El Paso which produced a wind gust up to 73 mph.
episodes.186187: Heavy rainfall caused flooding in Brevard County and roadway damage in Palm Bay.
episodes.186273: An area of low pressure that was moving slowly east across northern California into the Great Basin late September into the early October brought increased shower and thunderstorm chances to northeast California, the Sierra Front and eastern Sierra to include parts of western Nevada. This included high elevation snow showers over parts of the Sierra.
